scope: Documentary record of Indian coal block allocation: (1) the 1993-2011 screening-committee and government-dispensation allocations and their cancellation by the Supreme Court in 2014; (2) the statutory auction regime created in 2015 and the commercial-mining auction rounds from 2020; (3) per-block records for every commercially auctioned coal mine for which the Ministry of Coal has issued a vesting or allocation order. Descriptive only. No allegation of wrongdoing against any named company is made or implied anywhere in this file.

method.backbone: The per-block spine is the Ministry of Coal's own tranche-wise allocation file (allocation-trance-wise.pdf), updated through vesting orders dated 07.04.2026. It was downloaded with curl and its text extracted with pypdf; every row was parsed programmatically and the parse was checked row-by-row against the extracted text.
method.judgments: Both Supreme Court documents were taken from the Court's own server (api.sci.gov.in), not from a legal-database mirror. indiankanoon.org returned HTTP 403 to every automated request (both WebFetch and curl with a browser user-agent) and latestlaws.com returned 403 to curl and an empty body to WebFetch; neither was used.
method.cagReport: CAG Report No. 7 of 2012-13 is published on cag.gov.in as chapter-wise SCANNED PDFs with no text layer - pypdf extracted 11 characters from the 12 pages of Chapter 4. The chapters were therefore read as page images. Every CAG figure and quotation in this file was read off the page image of the printed report, not from a secondary account of it.
method.statutes: The Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015 and the MMDR Amendment Act 2015 were read from Gazette-of-India PDFs hosted by PRS Legislative Research. indiacode.nic.in redirected (HTTP 302 to an HTML interstitial) and legislative.gov.in returned 404 for the direct Act paths tried. The PRS files carry the Gazette masthead, registration number and publication date, and Schedule row counts were verified programmatically against the Act's own definition clauses.
method.identityResolution: Winner CINs were obtained from the GLEIF API by exact legal-name match with jurisdiction filtered to IN, and parent relationships from the GLEIF /direct-parent endpoint. Every CIN carries the basis on which it was matched. No CIN was guessed, and no CIN was constructed to build a registry URL.
method.nullPolicy: No figure, name, date, CIN, percentage or reserve in this file is estimated, inferred or recalled. Anything not read off a fetched document is null with a note and a corresponding gaps entry. Where two official documents disagree, both figures are carried and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.
method.nameNormalisation: The ministry's PDF extraction joins words ('Jindal Steeland Power Limited'). Winner names were normalised for whitespace only; winnerLegalNameAsPrinted preserves the ministry's text exactly, including its own misspellings ('NTPC Miniing Ltd', 'S M Steels and Powver Limited'), which are NOT corrected because correcting them would be an assertion about which company was meant.

screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.claim: For the period 1993 to 31 March 2011 the Union of India told the Supreme Court, on affidavit, that 216 coal block allocations had been made; the Attorney General added that 2 further blocks were allocated for Coal-to-Liquid projects, giving the 218 figure that circulates publicly.
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.exactWording: 'The Central Government in its first counter affidavit filed on 22.01.2013 has stated that for the period from 1993 to 31.03.2011, 216 allocations have been made. In the course of arguments, learned Attorney General submitted that in addition to 216, 2 coal blocks for Coal to Liquid (CTL) projects were also allocated. According to said affidavit, out of 216 allocations, 105 allocations were made to private companies, 99 allocations were made to Government companies and 12 allocations were made to Ultra Mega Power Projects (UMPPs) and that after adjusting 24 de-allocations and 2 re-allocations, a total number of 194 allocations, including allocations to private parties, remained.' (paragraph 106)
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.note: These are the Union government's own numbers as recorded by the Court, not the Court's findings. 105+99+12 = 216. The widely repeated '218' is 216 plus the 2 CTL blocks. The number that was actually live at the time of the judgment, on the government's own arithmetic, was 194.

screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.claim: On 25 August 2014 a bench of Chief Justice R.M. Lodha, Madan B. Lokur J and Kurian Joseph J held that the allocation of coal blocks on the recommendations of the Screening Committee across all 36 of its meetings from 14 July 1993, and the allocations made through the Government dispensation route, were arbitrary and illegal.
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.exactWording: '154. To sum up, the entire allocation of coal block as per recommendations made by the Screening Committee from 14.07.1993 in 36 meetings and the allocation through the Government dispensation route suffers from the vice of arbitrariness and legal flaws. The Screening Committee has never been consistent, it has not been transparent, there is no proper application of mind, it has acted on no material in many cases, relevant factors have seldom been its guiding factors... The approach had been ad-hoc and casual. There was no fair and transparent procedure, all resulting in unfair distribution of the national wealth. Common good and public interest have, thus, suffered heavily. Hence, the allocation of coal blocks based on the recommendations made in all the 36 meetings of the Screening Committee is illegal. 155. The allocation of coal blocks through Government dispensation route, however laudable the object may be, also is illegal since it is impermissible as per the scheme of the CMN Act.'
bench: R.M. Lodha, Chief Justice of India
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.note: The judgment did NOT cancel anything. It expressly left the consequences of the declaration open for further hearing (paragraph 157), which is why a second order was needed a month later. Reports that describe the 25 August judgment as having 'cancelled 204 blocks' compress two separate decisions into one.

screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.claim: The Ministry of Coal contested the CAG's inference; the CAG rejected the Ministry's contention, relying on the Ministry's own 2004-2006 record.
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.exactWording: The Ministry stated (February and March 2012) that 'The inference that the Government wanted to tap a part of it through competitive bidding appeared to be based on incomplete appreciation of the circumstances prevailing then and sequence of events thereafter', that 'The coal produced from captive blocks was not available for commercial sale', and that 'There would not be any gain to allottees as CIL was not in a position to supply additional coal to the allottees.' Audit replied: 'Secretary (Coal) had then stated that the competitive bidding procedure will only tap part of the profit that accrued to the companies which were allocated captive coal blocks under the screening committee procedure for public purposes... It was thus clear that MOC itself had acknowledged that there was gain to the allottees of coal blocks.'
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.denial: The Ministry of Coal's objection is reproduced in full in the audit report itself and is recorded here as the denial. The Coal Producers Association separately told the Supreme Court that the Rs 295 figure was unjustified, that the CAG report was contested by the Government and pending before a Parliamentary Committee on Public Undertakings, and that 'the Report itself suggested that only a part of the financial gain could have accrued to the national exchequer'.
screeningCommitteeEraAndCancellation.note: The Coal Producers Association's characterisation of the report, made to the Court, is accurate on this point - the report does say only a part could have been tapped. The Supreme Court accepted the Rs 295 figure anyway, expressly acknowledging its limits: 'It may well be that the cost of extraction of coal from an underground mine has not been taken into consideration by the CAG, but in matters of this nature it is difficult to arrive at any mathematically acceptable figure quantifying the loss sustained.'

auctionRegime.claim: The Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015 (Act 11 of 2015) is the statute that gave legal effect to the cancellation and created the re-allocation machinery. Its Schedule I - the operative list of cancelled mines - contains exactly 204 entries.

definitions.additionalLevy: 'additional levy' means, the additional levy as determined by the Supreme Court in Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 120 of 2012 as two hundred and ninety-five rupees per metric tonne of coal extracted
definitions.scheduleICoalMines: 'Schedule I coal mines' means, (i) all the coal mines and coal blocks the allocation of which was cancelled by the judgment dated 25th August, 2014 and its order dated 24th September, 2014 passed in Writ Petition (Criminal) No.120 of 2012, including those allotments which may have been de-allocated prior to and during the pendency of the said Writ Petition
definitions.scheduleIICoalMines: 'Schedule II coal mines' means the forty-two Schedule I coal mines listed in Schedule II which are the coal mines in relation to which the order of the Supreme Court dated 24th day of September, 2014 was made
definitions.scheduleIIICoalMines: 'Schedule III coal mines' means the thirty-two Schedule I coal mines listed in Schedule III or any other Schedule I coal mine as may be notified under sub-section (2) of section 7
definitions.priorAllottee: 'prior allottee' means prior allottee of Schedule I coal mines as listed therein who had been allotted coal mines between 1993 and 31st day of March, 2011, whose allotments have been cancelled pursuant to the judgment of the Supreme Court dated the 25th August, 2014 and its order dated 24th September, 2014 including those allotments which may have been de-allocated prior to and during the pendency of the Writ Petition (Criminal) No.120 of 2012.

auctionRegime.note: THIS IS WHERE 204 COMES FROM. Schedule I was parsed programmatically from the Gazette text: its serial numbers run 1 to 204 with no gaps, ending at '204 East of Damogoria (Kalyaneshwari), West Bengal Power Development Corporation Limited (WBPDCL), West Bengal'. Schedule II likewise runs 1 to 42 and Schedule III 1 to 32, matching the Act's own definitions ('the forty-two...', 'the thirty-two...') exactly. Schedule I is broader than the set the Court cancelled on 24 September 2014, because clause 3(1)(p)(i) expressly sweeps in blocks that had already been de-allocated before or during the writ petition. So 204 is not '218 minus 14'; it is a statutory list assembled on its own definition.

auctionRegime.claim: The bid parameter in commercial coal auctions is a percentage share of revenue, not a rupee price. There is therefore no contract value for any commercial coal award, and any table that sums 'value awarded' for these mines is summing something that does not exist.
auctionRegime.eliminationRule: Technically Qualified Bidders are ranked on their Initial Offers. If 2 to 3 TQBs, all qualify; if 4 to 6, the lowest-ranked is eliminated; if 7 or more, the lowest-ranked one-third subject to a maximum of 3 are eliminated. No TQB is eliminated if that would leave fewer than 3 Qualified Bidders. The auction process is annulled if there are fewer than 2 TQBs.
auctionRegime.note: The annulment rule is the reason 'blocks offered' and 'blocks auctioned' diverge so widely: a mine attracting one qualified bidder is not awarded cheaply, it is not awarded at all. That is a designed-in feature, and it means an unsuccessful tranche is evidence of thin participation rather than of a captured process.

whyThisIsNotTheOnlyDenominator.explanation: The Ministry of Coal's May 2026 pre-bid presentation states that 140 coal blocks have been auctioned across 14 tranches. The tranche-wise allocation file, updated through vesting orders dated 07.04.2026, lists 133. A block is 'auctioned' when a successful bidder is declared; it appears in the tranche-wise file only once a vesting or allocation order has issued, which requires payment of the upfront amount, the fixed amount and submission of performance security. The 7-block gap is therefore expected, not anomalous - but it means the two counts must never be mixed, and any percentage computed on one must not be quoted against the other.

corporateFamilyCaveat.innocentReading: Large diversified groups bid through the operating subsidiary that will consume the coal, because the CM(SP) Act auction has no end-use restriction but the group's internal logistics do. A cement company bidding through its cement arm and a power company through its power arm is ordinary corporate structuring, not concealment. Nothing in the entity naming here supports an inference of disguise.

corporateFamilyCaveat.killIf: The group-level top-5 share turns out to be close to the entity-level 20.30 per cent, in which case entity fragmentation was never doing analytical work.

Only the sheets for rounds 10, 11 and 12 were still on the Nominated Authority's download page when it was fetched; sheets for rounds 1-9 and 13-14 were not, so the statistics below describe three consecutive recent rounds and MUST NOT be read as the distribution for the programme.
revenueShareOutcomes.reading: Across the 25 mine-wise final offers that could be sourced, the winning revenue share ranges from 5.50 per cent to 79.00 per cent against a 4 per cent floor - a fourteen-fold spread within three consecutive rounds. Four awards cleared at 6 per cent or below and five above 30 per cent. A percentage revenue share is not a price and these numbers are not comparable across mines: a high share on a small, poor-grade, remote block and a low share on a large, high-grade block can represent identical economics. Ranking companies by the revenue share they bid would be a category error.

baseRates.denominatorLabel: 133 commercially auctioned coal blocks with a vesting or allocation order to 07.04.2026; 81 distinct winning legal entities
baseRates.reading: 20.30 per cent. On the evidence-tiering scale this sits in the 10-40 per cent 'moderate' band, and the top winner alone holds 6.02 per cent. The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index on block share is 195, which for reference is far below the 1,500 threshold conventionally treated as the boundary of an unconcentrated market. Whatever else is true of this programme, award concentration by legal entity is low, and any claim that a small set of firms has captured commercial coal auctions has to be made against this number.
baseRates.innocentReading: Coal blocks are lumpy assets and some firms have several end-use plants, so a firm winning 6 or 8 of 133 blocks over six years is unremarkable. Rungta Sons, the top winner, is a Kolkata company incorporated in 1943 (CIN U02005WB1943PTC011231) - a long-established mining house, not a new entrant.

baseRates.reading: ZERO of the 133 blocks in this file has a published bidder count. The Nominated Authority publishes a list of Technically Qualified Bidders per tranche and a result sheet giving the winning bid, but does not publish how many bidders competed for each mine. This is a documented void and it is load-bearing: without it, no statement about whether any particular award was competitive can be made, in either direction. The one thing that IS known is structural - the tender rules annul the auction for any mine with fewer than two technically qualified bidders, so every awarded mine had at least two.

gaps: DISTRICT is null for all 133 blocks. No Ministry of Coal document opened in this pass publishes the district of a coal block. The tranche-wise allocation file gives the state; the CMPDI technical presentations give the coalfield (Mand-Raigarh, Talcher, Rajmahal, Sohagpur, North Karanpura, Ib Valley, Wardha Valley, Korba, Singrauli, Kamptee, Pench Kanhan, Bishrampur, Tatapani-Ramkola, Umaria, Umrer, Auranga, Godavari Valley, Namchik Namphuk, Bander, Palana Basin, Bikaner, Sendurgarh, Mahaloi). District appears in the per-mine 'mine dossier' sold with the tender document, which is not free to download. Coalfield-to-district is a many-to-many mapping and was NOT inferred.

GEOLOGICAL RESERVES are populated for only 24 of the 126 ministry rows. Reserves are published per block in the CMPDI pre-bid technical presentation and the upfront-amount notice for each tranche, but the Nominated Authority's download page carries only the documents for recent rounds - in practice rounds 11 to 15. For rounds 1 to 10 (roughly 100 blocks) no reserves document is reachable. Reserves were NOT back-filled from any secondary source.

MINE-WISE FINAL OFFER (revenue share) is populated for 25 of 133 blocks - rounds 10, 11 and 12 only, from the Nominated Authority's own one-page result sheets. Result sheets for rounds 1 to 9 and 13 to 14 are no longer on the download page that was fetched.

BIDDER COUNT PER MINE is not published for any of the 133 blocks by any source reached. The Ministry of Coal publishes a per-tranche list of Technically Qualified Bidders and a per-mine winning bid, but never the number of bids received for a given mine. This is the largest single hole in the file and it bounds what can be said about competition.
RESERVE PRICE per mine was not obtained for rounds 10-12. The result sheets published for those rounds give only the closing bid, not the reserve price against which it should be read.

CIN is null for 15 of the 81 distinct winning entities, and for 60 of the 126 ministry rows. GLEIF holds LEI records only for entities that have obtained one, which is overwhelmingly the larger and the borrowing companies. The unresolved entities are almost entirely the small single-block private winners - which is precisely the part of the distribution that most needs resolving, since a family of related shell entities winning several blocks each under different names would be invisible in the entity-level distribution published here. No CIN was guessed and no MCA mirror URL was constructed without one.
J.K. Cement Ltd. (2 blocks) and Bharat Aluminium Company Ltd (1 block) returned no matching Indian legal-entity record from GLEIF's exact-name endpoint; their CINs are null.

OFFERED COUNTS for rounds 1 to 10 could not be sourced. The Ministry of Coal's tranche-wise summary publishes only the number successfully auctioned. Round 12's offered count is recorded as printed but is internally inconsistent in the ministry's own slide ('28 (26+2)' total against '25 (23+2)' current plus '03' second-attempt).

The CAG's Annexures III, IV and V - the per-block tables underlying the Rs 1,85,591.34 crore figure, naming each of the 57 private opencast/mixed mines and its extractable reserve - are in the annexures PDF, which is also a scanned image without a text layer. They were NOT transcribed. Anyone wanting the company-level breakdown of the CAG's computed gain must read that file page by page.

The 25 August 2014 judgment was read for its holdings, its counts and its Screening Committee findings, but its 117 pages were not exhaustively transcribed; per-company findings inside it may exist that this file does not carry.

indiankanoon.org returned HTTP 403 to every request, from both WebFetch and curl with a browser user-agent (Cloudflare interstitial, 'Just a moment...'). latestlaws.com returned HTTP 403 to curl and served WebFetch a page containing only the case title. Neither was used as a source. The Supreme Court's own api.sci.gov.in served both judgments without difficulty and is the better route.

indiacode.nic.in returned HTTP 302 to an HTML interstitial for the direct Act PDF paths, and legislative.gov.in returned 404. The statutes were read from the Gazette PDFs hosted by PRS Legislative Research, which carry the Gazette masthead and registration number. This is a reproduction of a primary record rather than the record served by its issuing department, and it is flagged as such.
bombayhighcourt.nic.in (an alternative government host for the CMSP Act) timed out after 90 seconds.

mstcecommerce.com, the auction platform itself, was NOT reached in this pass. The MSTC bidder registration numbers recorded on 20 winners come from the Ministry of Coal's own result sheets, not from MSTC.

OPERATIONAL STATUS is not established for any block. The tranche-wise file records that a vesting or allocation order issued; it does not record whether the mine has since opened, produced, been terminated or been surrendered. The status field on every block record says exactly that and nothing more. The Ministry of Coal's February 2026 notice confirms that a Scrutiny Committee mechanism for milestone failures exists and is used, so terminations do occur, but no list of them was reachable.

PARTY, DONATION AND POLITICAL LINKAGE: none is recorded, because none was researched. This file is an allocation register. Any inference from it to political financing would need a separate dataset and a separate denominator.

The 204 entries in Schedule I of the CMSP Act were counted programmatically and their range verified (1 to 204, no gaps), but the 204 prior-allottee names in that schedule were NOT transcribed into this file. That schedule is the authoritative list of who held the cancelled blocks and is the obvious next dataset.

No control set was run. The symmetry check in the pattern-discipline skill would require running the identical concentration analysis on a comparable auctioned-resource programme - state mineral blocks, or the pre-2015 captive tranches - and comparing. That was not done, so the 20.30 per cent top-5 figure has no benchmark other than the HHI reference value.

rejected.candidate: 'The Supreme Court cancelled 204 of 218 coal blocks'
rejected.reason: Neither number appears in either Supreme Court document. The 24 September 2014 order works with 46 blocks, of which it quashes 42 and saves 4; all remaining allocations are quashed without being counted. 204 is the number of rows in Schedule I of the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015, a statutory list defined more broadly than the Court's order because it expressly includes blocks already de-allocated before the writ. 218 is 216 (the Union's affidavit figure for 1993 to 31.03.2011) plus 2 Coal-to-Liquid blocks mentioned by the Attorney General in argument. The sentence fuses a parliamentary schedule, a government affidavit and an oral submission and attributes the result to a court.

rejected.candidate: 'The CAG found a loss of Rs 1.86 lakh crore to the exchequer'
rejected.reason: The report says the opposite in terms. Paragraph 4.3 is headed 'Financial gains to the private parties' and states a 'financial gain of Rs 185,591.34 crore to private parties in respect of 57 OC/Mixed mines as on 31 March, 2011', followed by 'A part of this financial gain could have been tapped by the Government'. A gain to a private party of which only a part was capturable is not a loss to the exchequer, and the report never quantifies the capturable part.

rejected.candidate: Folding Jindal Power Limited and Jindal Steel and Power Limited into a single 11-block winner
rejected.reason: GLEIF's direct-parent record for Jindal Power Limited (LEI 335800RV5JVZCX7F1657) names AMBITIOUS ASSET PRIVATE LIMITED (U74999DL2021PTC384075), not Jindal Steel and Power Limited. The merge would have been a name-match entity-resolution failure and would have produced the file's largest winner and a materially more concentrated top-5.

rejected.candidate: Correcting 'S M Steels and Powver Limited' to 'S M Steels and Power Limited'
rejected.reason: Two independent Ministry of Coal documents - the tranche-wise allocation file and the 10th-round result sheet - both print 'Powver'. The misspelling is the government's, is consistent across documents, and correcting it would be an assertion about which company was meant. It is preserved verbatim and flagged.

rejected.candidate: Merging 'Shreesatya Mine Private Limited' and 'Shreesatya Mines Private Limited'
rejected.reason: The ministry file prints both, on different rows, for different mines (Rauta Closed and Burakhap Small Patch). Whether this is one entity misspelled once or two entities is not established. They are counted separately, which if anything understates concentration by one block - recorded here so the direction of the error is known.

rejected.candidate: Attributing a group to Mahan Energen Ltd from its Gujarat registered office
rejected.reason: The registered office is circumstantial. The attribution in this file rests on the GLEIF direct-parent record naming ADANI POWER LIMITED (L40100GJ1996PLC030533), which is a registry relationship, not an address coincidence. The source-retrieval discipline is explicit that a shared or suggestive address is never a filing.

rejected.candidate: Summing a rupee 'value awarded' across commercial coal auctions
rejected.reason: There is no rupee bid. The bid parameter is a percentage share of revenue, and the rupee amounts that do exist (upfront amount, fixed amount, bid security) are computed from geological reserves and cost recovery, not bid. Any total 'value' figure for this programme is constructed.

Out of scope and, more importantly, expressly outside the 2014 judgment: 'the judgment delivered on 25th August, 2014 does not concern lignite blocks at all and their allotments are not covered by the said judgment' (order of 24 September 2014, paragraph 12). Two lignite blocks in Rajasthan appeared in the 12th-round offer list and are noted but not recorded as coal blocks.

rejected.candidate: Ranking winners by the revenue-share percentage they bid
rejected.reason: A revenue share is not a price. The observed range within three consecutive rounds is 5.50 to 79.00 per cent, and it varies with reserve size, grade, method of mining and evacuation distance. Comparing a 79 per cent bid on a 36 Mt Maharashtra block with a 5.5 per cent bid on an 891 Mt Odisha block as if one were more or less aggressive than the other is a category error.

rejected.candidate: The 57 allotted (non-auctioned) blocks and the 19 pre-commercial auctioned blocks, in the concentration figures
rejected.reason: Allotment to government companies is a different statutory route with no bidding, and the pre-commercial auctions were end-use restricted. Including either would mix award mechanisms. Their counts are carried in denominators.otherDenominatorsInThisFile so the reader can see what was excluded and how large it is.
